documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual visit, 43 next month. Feels a bit more winded than last year - stairs at work slower, tired by the evening. Sleeps flat. No swelling, no chest pain, palpitations only now and then. INRs at the clinic in range per her. Cardiology appointment is April 15.

Meds: HCTZ 25 daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, warfarin 5 mg (anticoag clinic). NKDA.
PHQ-2: 1.

Exam: vitals as charted. No JVD. Regular rhythm, loud S1, apical diastolic rumble. Lungs clear. No edema. Breasts without masses.

A/P:
1. Severe rheumatic MS with chronic HF, PAF on warfarin: somewhat more exertional symptoms; keep the April cardiology visit and ask them to send us the note.
2. CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c.
3. Screening mammogram ordered. Pap/HPV due 2026.
4. Colon cancer screening starts at 45; we will set it up next year.
Return in 4 months.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs from the physical are all normal. Please don't forget the mammogram and your heart appointment next month.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 04/2022 and 11/2020. Heterogeneously dense tissue. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion. No interval change.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative mammogram, BI-RADS 1. Patient notified through the portal.

conditions.label: Pulmonary hypertension due to mitral stenosis
conditions.note: WHO group 2; PASP 56 mmHg on echo

reports.text: PA and lateral. Mild enlargement of the left atrium. Redistribution of pulmonary vascular markings toward the upper lobes. No effusion, consolidation or pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Mild left atrial enlargement with pulmonary vascular redistribution.

reports.text: Comparison 10/2022. Rheumatic mitral valve with commissural fusion. Mitral valve area 0.9 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 13 mmHg at a heart rate of 104. LA volume index 58 mL/m2. LV normal size, LVEF 60%. Right ventricle mildly dilated with preserved systolic function. Estimated PA systolic pressure 56 mmHg. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, MVA 0.9 cm2, mean gradient 13 mmHg. Estimated PASP 56 mmHg; mildly dilated RV with preserved function. LVEF 60%.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group - follow-up note (faxed on request)
Visit date: 04/15/2024

She is back for her rheumatic mitral stenosis, first seen here in October 2022 for progressive exertional dyspnea and fatigue. Her exertional breathlessness and tiredness have crept up over the last several years, and she now needs extra pillows at night. She reports taking hydrochlorothiazide every day as directed.

Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, potassium chloride 20 mEq daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, warfarin 5 mg daily (INR 2-3).
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: HR 104, RR 21, BP 112/82. Loud S1 with a prominent opening snap after S2 and a low rumbling diastolic murmur at the apex late in diastole. Palpable RV lift at the left sternal border. No JVD. No peripheral edema. Lungs clear.

Chest x-ray: mild left atrial enlargement, redistribution of pulmonary vascular markings.
Echo: MVA 0.9 cm2, mean gradient 13 mmHg at HR 104, LAVI 58 mL/m2, LVEF 60%, RV mildly dilated with normal function, PASP 56 mmHg.

Impression:
1. Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, progressing.
2. Pulmonary hypertension due to mitral stenosis (WHO group 2).
3. Chronic heart failure, new orthopnea.
4. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin.

Plan: no medication changes today. Continue sodium restriction. Follow up in cardiology.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Follow-up. Breathing has been worse since spring. Walks slowly, rests partway up a flight of stairs, and for a couple of months has slept on two pillows because lying flat makes her short of breath. No chest pain. No ankle swelling. Occasional flutters. No bleeding. She saw cardiology on April 15; she was told the pressure in her lungs is up from the valve and to keep cutting salt, no medicine changes. We do not have that note - requesting it today.

Meds: HCTZ 25 daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, warfarin 5 mg per anticoag clinic. NKDA.

O: Vitals as charted. Comfortable at rest. No JVD. Loud S1, apical diastolic rumble. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with chronic HF, now orthopnea; pulmonary pressure elevated per cardiology (report pending). Records request to cardiology sent. Continue current regimen and 2 g sodium. She knows to go to the ED for breathlessness at rest or chest pain.
2. PAF on warfarin, anticoag clinic managing.
3. BMP and CBC today.
Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Hospital emergency department - physician record (received by fax 4/21/2026)
Date of service: 3/31/2026

CC: short of breath, heart racing, cough.

HPI: 45-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis and pulmonary hypertension followed by cardiology, brought in after a few hours of rapidly increasing breathlessness with palpitations and a cough that kept getting worse.

PMH: rheumatic fever in childhood; rheumatic mitral stenosis; pulmonary hypertension; chronic heart failure; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
PSH: tonsillectomy at 8.
Home meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, warfarin 5 mg daily (INR 2-3), potassium chloride 20 mEq daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother rheumatic fever; father type 2 diabetes; maternal uncle stroke at 65.
SH: administrative assistant; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: BP 130/85, HR 120 and irregularly irregular, RR 22, SpO2 92% on room air. Diastolic rumble at the apex, heard best in left lateral decubitus. Crackles at both bases.

ECG: atrial fibrillation, rapid rate, no ST changes.
CXR: left atrial enlargement, elevated left mainstem bronchus, interstitial edema.
Labs: NT-proBNP 2860 pg/mL; hs-troponin I 9 ng/L; INR 2.4; Na 137, K 3.7, Cr 0.84; Hgb 12.4, WBC 7.6.

ED course: oxygen 2 L by nasal cannula with SpO2 to 96%. Furosemide 40 mg IV. Metoprolol tartrate 5 mg IV twice for rate control. Warfarin therapeutic, held tonight pending inpatient team.

Impression: acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema; atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; severe rheumatic mitral stenosis.
Disposition: admitted to cardiology telemetry.

events.reason: acute decompensated heart failure, atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

reports.text: Comparison 04/2024. Rheumatic mitral valve with commissural fusion. Mitral valve area 0.8 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 14 mmHg at a heart rate of 78, sinus rhythm. LVEF 60%. Estimated PA systolic pressure 62 mmHg. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, MVA 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 14 mmHg. Estimated PASP 62 mmHg. LVEF 60%.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Hospital discharge summary (received 8/11/2026 after patient request)
Admitted 3/31/2026, discharged 4/3/2026. Service: inpatient cardiology.

Principal diagnosis: acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema.
Secondary: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; severe rheumatic mitral stenosis; pulmonary hypertension due to mitral stenosis.

Course: Admitted from the ED after IV furosemide and IV metoprolol. Diuresed with IV furosemide with steady improvement in breathing; off oxygen by day 2. Converted on her own to sinus rhythm on 4/1. Warfarin resumed, INR stayed therapeutic. Echo 4/1: MVA 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 14 mmHg at HR 78, PASP 62 mmHg, LVEF 60%.

Discharge medications:
- Furosemide 40 mg by mouth daily (NEW)
- Metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily (INCREASED from 50 mg)
- Warfarin 5 mg daily, INR goal 2-3 (continue; anticoagulation clinic)
- Potassium chloride 20 mEq daily (continue)
- Hydrochlorothiazide: STOPPED
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: referred to the structural heart program for evaluation for percutaneous balloon mitral valvotomy; INR check within a week; primary care follow-up in 1 to 2 weeks.

documents.title: Pharmacy call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacist called: patient filled new furosemide 40 mg daily and metoprolol succinate 100 mg from a hospital discharge on 4/3, and an auto-refill for HCTZ 25 (our Rx) is also queued. Asked whether HCTZ should still be filled. Called pt - she says the hospital told her to stop HCTZ. Told pharmacy to cancel the HCTZ refill. We have no hospital records; requested discharge summary and ED record from the hospital. PCP aware.

documents.title: was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to tell you I was in the hospital at the end of March for 3 days, fluid in my lungs and my heart went into the fast irregular rhythm. They gave me a different water pill and a higher metoprolol and stopped the hydrochlorothiazide. Now they want me to see a valve team about fixing the valve with a balloon. I'm feeling much better.

documents.title: RE: was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, and I'm glad you are feeling better. We have asked the hospital for your records. Please book a visit with me in the next week or two so we can go over your medicines and check your blood work - the front desk can find you a time.

documents.title: Structural Heart Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Structural heart program - consultation letter
Visit date: 5/19/2026

46-year-old woman with severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, pulmonary hypertension and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin, hospitalized 3/31-4/3/2026 for decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema and AF with rapid rates. Since discharge her breathing is better: she walks a block and takes stairs slowly. Sinus rhythm today.

Meds: furosemide 40 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily, warfarin 5 mg daily (INR 2-3), potassium chloride 20 mEq daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Review of echoes 2022, 2024 and 4/2026: progressive severe rheumatic MS, MVA now 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 14 mmHg, PASP 62 mmHg, LVEF 60%. Valve anatomy suitable for a balloon approach.

Recommendation: percutaneous balloon mitral valvotomy, preceded by a transesophageal echo to exclude left atrial thrombus. Continue warfarin and the current regimen. Our office will schedule.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.

documents.title: valve procedure done
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doctor, I had the balloon procedure on my valve last Tuesday, July 21. Went home the next day. I can already breathe easier walking. They said they will send you the report. I still need to make my appointment with you, sorry.

documents.title: RE: valve procedure done
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is wonderful news. We have not received the report yet and will ask for it. Please do come in when you can - I would like to see you and catch up on everything since 2024.
